question: The temperature at which air becomes saturated with water vapour is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __Dew Point Temperature**(Dew Point)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dew Point Temperature__ is the temperature at which air becomes saturated with water vapour.
 
• At this temperature, air can no longer hold water vapour, causing it to condense into liquid water.
 
• Dew point is an essential measure for humidity levels in the atmosphere.
 
• Higher dew points indicate more moisture in the air, whereas lower dew points indicate dry air.
 
• The dew point is used in weather forecasting to understand comfort levels and precipitation likelihood.
 
• It is not the same as wet bulb or dry bulb temperature measurements.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Wet Bulb Temperature:**

 
 
• It is the lowest temperature that can be achieved by evaporative cooling of air.
 
• It is an indicator of humidity and is used in HVAC and meteorological studies.
 
 
 
• **Dry Bulb Temperature:**
 
 
• It is the temperature of air measured by a standard thermometer.
 
• It does not take into account the moisture content in the air.
 
 
 
• **Wet Bulb Depression:**
 
 
• The difference between dry bulb and wet bulb temperatures.
 
• It is used to determine relative humidity.
